title: Evolutionary-scale prediction of atomic level protein structure with a language model
layout_note: Only panel A is the method (B-D are results plots and structure comparisons). Left: a sequence pill ('EGRLTVYCTVQ...', labelled Single Sequence) feeds a row of token squares into a large stacked ESM-2 block, whose output token row sits on top ('Pretrained via Masked LM'); lines from the sequence and from the top token row meet at a circled-plus junction that feeds Folding Trunk (48 blocks) -> Structure Module (8 blocks) -> a rendered cartoon of the predicted structure, with a 'Recycling' line running back over the top from the structure to the trunk. To the right, unconnected, the Folding Block is opened as a detail panel: Pair Rep and Seq Rep enter a rounded container from the left as two horizontal lanes and leave at the right.
grouping: No containers in the overview; repetition is shown by stacking three to four offset copies of each block with the block count written underneath. The detail panel is one pale-pink rounded rectangle titled beneath ('Folding Block'); inside it the pair lane runs along the top and the sequence lane along the bottom, joined by vertical arrows (pair -> Bias -> Self attention; sequence Transition -> up into Pairwise product / difference).
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with soft fills (saturated red for ESM-2, mauve trunk, peach structure module; pale yellow-green and grey-green sub-blocks in the detail) and thin grey outlines; stacked cards give the repeated blocks a pseudo-depth. Tokens are rows of small empty squares inside a rounded pill. The pair representation is a small blue heatmap square, the sequence representation a thin blue striped bar. The output is a rendered teal cartoon protein with one magenta segment. Thin black arrows.
proposed_highlight: The language model is the largest and only saturated block (a big red stacked deck with 'ESM-2' in large type), so the reading starts there; the folding block is unpacked in its own panel on the right rather than inside the pipeline.
lesson: Represent the two tracks by their data shapes - a small square heatmap for 'Pair Rep' and a thin strip for 'Seq Rep' - and run them as two horizontal lanes through the block detail, with vertical arrows only where one track writes into the other.
notes: Venue = bioRxiv preprint: the PDF header reads 'bioRxiv preprint doi: 10.1101/2022.07.20.500902; this version posted December 21, 2022' (v3; venue_source: pdf); no journal version was checked. Measured on a trimmed copy of panel A only (crops/esmfold/fig2a.png = the top 352 px of fig2.png, with the sliver of panel D at its lower right painted white), because panels B-D are results. The whole figure is one embedded raster, so photo_share is null and the rendered protein's teal is part of the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: single-sequence protein structure prediction from a language model
taxonomy.note: only panel A is the method (B-D are results); crop opened from the build cache at kb-build/protein-structure/crops/esmfold/fig2a.png because kb fetch-crop had no recipe

core.what: panel A's one-row pipeline from a quoted single sequence through a large saturated red ESM-2 deck, a mauve Folding Trunk stack and a peach Structure Module stack to a rendered protein, with a 'Recycling' line back over the top

relations.form: left to right in panel A: sequence string 'EGRLTVYCTVQ...' below ESM-2 rising into it, ESM-2 out to a circled plus, then Folding Trunk (48 blocks) -> Structure Module (8 blocks) -> 'Predicted structure and confidence' as a teal ribbon render
a line from the input sequence runs round the right of ESM-2 and joins its output at a circled plus before the Folding Trunk
a thin 'Recycling' line runs from the rendered structure up and back left over the row into the top of the Folding Trunk; blocks are drawn as offset stacked cards with counts underneath

a separate pale-pink rounded panel to the right, titled 'Folding Block' underneath, opens one trunk block as two horizontal lanes: a pair-representation heat-map tile on the upper lane and a sequence-representation strip on the lower lane, crossing through Bias, Self attention, Transition, Pairwise product/difference and Triangular Update
the rest of the figure (B-D) holds results, not method: bar charts and scatter plots comparing ESMFold with AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold, calibration scatters, and superposed structure renders

channels.colour: in panel A colour = module identity (saturated red = ESM-2, mauve = trunk, peach = structure module, pale yellow/green = operations inside the folding block); the folding-block panel's pale pink only loosely echoes the mauve trunk; in B-D blue = ESMFold bars and a blue-red ramp = perplexity, so blue is used for both a method and a low-perplexity value
channels.shape: stacked offset cards = repeated blocks, row of small squares = token sequence, heat-map tile = pair representation, ribbon render = structure
channels.line: thin black arrows for data; one long thin line for recycling
channels.frame: a rounded tinted panel = the inside of one folding block; ESM-2's token rows sit in rounded outlined boxes

quality.strengths: ESM-2 is by far the largest and most saturated element, so the reader starts at the language model the paper is about; the folding block draws the pair and sequence representations as data (a heat-map tile and a strip) on two lanes that cross where they interact; the output is a real rendered protein.
quality.weaknesses: The method is compressed into the top third of a figure dominated by results panels; the folding-block zoom is tied to the trunk only by a loose tint and its title, with no callout; the sequence bypass line bends round ESM-2 and the recycling line spans the full row; the folding block's internal arrows are small and unordered relative to its title placed below it.

insights.structure: Left, the pipeline ESM-2 -> Folding Trunk -> Structure Module -> rendered protein runs unframed in one row; right, a separate pale-pink rounded panel titled 'Folding Block' beneath opens one trunk block as two horizontal lanes.
insights.data: The input is a pill with the literal string 'EGRLTVYCTVQ...' and rows of empty token squares; repeated blocks are 3-4 offset stacked cards with '48 blocks' / '8 blocks' beneath; Pair Rep is a small blue heatmap square and Seq Rep a thin striped strip; the output is a teal cartoon protein.
insights.emphasis: ESM-2 is the largest and only saturated block (a big red stacked deck with large type), so the reader starts at the language model; the rest is muted mauve, peach and pale green.
insights.flow: Bottom-left sequence goes up through ESM-2, joins at a circled-plus, then runs left-to-right to the structure, with a 'Recycling' line arching back over the top to the trunk; in the detail panel vertical arrows mark where pair and sequence lanes write into each other.
insights.avoid: The Folding Block panel has no connector or zoom cue back to the Folding Trunk stack, and the circled-plus junction where the raw sequence and ESM-2 output merge is unlabeled.

arrangement.units: unframed pipeline row plus one framed pale-pink detail panel for the Folding Block placed beside it
arrangement.inputs_as: rounded pill with a literal amino-acid string and a token-square row
